title: De V2-regel — werkwoord op plek twee
summary: Present-tense conjugation and verb-second: front anything, the verb stays in slot 2

blocks.title: Present tense: stem + endings
blocks.body: Take the infinitive (*werken* = to work), drop *-en* to get the **stem** (*werk*). Then: *ik* adds nothing, *jij* and *hij/zij* add **-t**, and the plurals (*wij/jullie/zij*) just use the full infinitive again. That's the whole system.

blocks.title: Hear the forms of wonen (to live)
Keep the vowel sound: woon, not won
blocks.body: One spelling reflex. *wonen* has a long 'oo' sound. Drop *-en* and you'd get *won* — but a single vowel in a closed syllable goes short. To **keep the long sound**, double it: the *ik*-form is *woon*. Same reason *maken* → *ik maak*.
blocks.callout: Flip side: *pakken* → *ik pak*. A short vowel drops the doubled consonant.

blocks.explain: *jij* takes the stem + **-t**: *jij woont*. Only *ik* gets the bare stem.

blocks.title: The law: the verb is second
blocks.body: In a Dutch main clause the finite verb sits in **position two** — always. Not second *word*, second *slot*. In the plainest sentence, slot 1 is the subject and slot 2 is the verb: *Ik drink koffie.* Nothing surprising yet — the magic is what happens when you move something to the front.
blocks.callout: Count constituents, not words: 's ochtends is one slot, however long it is.

blocks.title: Front something, and the subject flips behind the verb
blocks.body: Put a time or place first and the verb **stays** in slot 2 — so the subject gets bumped to slot 3. This flip (inversion) is not optional; it's the law holding. Same verb, same slot, every time:

pairs.note: Move *vandaag* to the front and *ik* jumps behind the verb. The verb never moves off slot 2.
Front the time, invert the subject. English keeps 'we eat'; Dutch cannot.

blocks.explain: Front *vandaag*, keep the verb in slot 2, subject behind it: *Vandaag werk ik…*. The English-style 'Vandaag ik werk' breaks V2.

blocks.title: Build a V2 sentence — one slot per position
blocks.prompt: Fill the four positions in order. The verb must land in slot 2, so pick your front element first and let the subject fall behind the verb.
Rewrite starting with the time. Base sentence: 'Ik ga om negen uur naar mijn werk.' Start with 'Om negen uur …'.
answers: Om negen uur ga ik naar mijn werk
blocks.hint: Verb stays second, so *ga* comes right after the time, then *ik*.
blocks.explain: *Om negen uur ga ik naar mijn werk.* Front the time → verb in slot 2 → subject inverts.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the V2 sentence.
Write three sentences about your day, each starting with a different front element (a time, a place, a day). Check that your verb sits in slot 2 every time.
